page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-4GB is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 shared vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate that the shared CPU allocation and hardware profile constrain performance. The instance registers poor multi-core and single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the bottom 10% of benchmarks. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read and write operations falling into the bottom 10%, while small-block cached reads perform in the bottom 25%. Geekbench results show average single-core performance in the middle 50% and weak multi-core performance in the bottom 25%, with similar weak results in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing.

Due to the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this server exhibits significant performance tradeoffs under sustained compute and memory-intensive workloads, as evidenced by its poor static web serving throughput and weak database operations. However, it maintains average performance in text processing and bzip3 single-threaded decompression. This resource profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic text processing, low-traffic web serving, or small-scale development and testing environments that do not require dedicated CPU resources or high memory bandwidth.
